title: Evaluating Generative Models via Cubical Homology based Persistent Entropy

problem.claim: Generative-model evaluation can use topological properties to assess the diversity and quality of generated data.

gap.claim: Existing topological methods are impractical for higher-dimensional settings and large-scale datasets or models.

contributions.claim: A scalable framework based on persistent entropy for evaluating generative models.
A theoretical relation between the homological complexity of underlying topology and persistent entropy.
An empirical study of topological transformation during training of the generated data manifold using cubical homology.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method is reported to be domain- and model-agnostic.
The method is reported to scale well across various neural architectures and depths.

narrative_sequence.summary: Topological tools are used to study the relationship between generative-model representation power and topological properties.
Existing methods do not scale practically to higher dimensions and large datasets or models.
The paper proposes a scalable persistent-entropy framework and establishes a theoretical relation to homological complexity.
The authors empirically study topological changes during training using cubical homology and report broad scalability.

source_observation.claim: Persistent entropy is related theoretically to the homological complexity of the underlying topology.

interpretation.claim: Entropy-based summaries may provide scalable proxies for topological complexity.

application.claim: Use persistent-entropy measures when evaluating generated-data structure across high-dimensional or large-scale settings.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the proxy is reliable or informative.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, metrics, quantitative results, or experimental conditions are specified.
No details are provided about the persistent-entropy formulation or cubical-homology implementation.
No limitations or failure cases are reported.
